A name declared at namespace scope can be used through qualification, such as harbor::limit, when its declaration is visible. Headers commonly use namespaces to organize interfaces shared across translation units. Namespace scope does not mean every declaration is mutable global state. A function declaration, a type, and a constexpr policy constant can all live there. Avoid broad using namespace directives in headers, because they change the name-lookup environment of every file that includes them. slides.title: 9.2.1 Understanding Automatic Storage Duration
keyPoints: Ordinary local objects usually have automatic storage duration: their storage is managed as execution enters and.
Construction establishes the object’s lifetime, and destruction ends it for class objects.
The standard’s storage-duration model is more precise than saying every local variable is physically on a stack.
Ordinary local objects usually have automatic storage duration: their storage is managed as execution enters and.
slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 9, use 9.2.1 Understanding Automatic Storage Duration as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Ordinary local objects usually have automatic storage duration: their storage is managed as execution enters and leaves the relevant block. Construction establishes the object’s lifetime, and destruction ends it for class objects. The standard’s storage-duration model is more precise than saying every local variable is physically on a stack; optimization can change placement or eliminate storage entirely. Returning a local object by value is safe because the result is a distinct returned value, with copy elision or movement available where applicable. Returning a pointer or reference to that same local object is not safe. The caller receives an access path to an object whose lifetime has ended, regardless of whether the old bytes remain unchanged for a while. The graduate-level move is to ask what evidence would make the claim trustworthy: a compiler diagnostic, a runtime value, a preserved invariant, or a boundary that failed cleanly. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 9, use 9.2.2 Understanding Static Storage Duration as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Objects with static storage duration have storage associated with the program’s execution rather than one ordinary block entry. A local static object is initialized when control first reaches its declaration, under the applicable initialization rules, and persists across later calls. Its name can remain block-local even though its lifetime is much longer. A mutable local static counter therefore remembers previous calls, which can be useful but introduces hidden state. Concurrent initialization of a function-local static is handled by the language, but subsequent unsynchronized mutation is not automatically safe. Static duration should not be confused with automatic thread safety or with a universal guarantee about initialization order across unrelated translation units. The graduate-level move is to ask what evidence would make the claim trustworthy: a compiler diagnostic, a runtime value, a preserved invariant, or a boundary that failed cleanly. slides.title: 9.3.1 Recognizing Lifetime-Related Bugs
keyPoints: A dangling pointer or reference does not become safe merely because it is nonnull.
It may point to an object that has been destroyed, a vector element invalidated by reallocation, or a temporary.
Checking the numeric address cannot reconstruct the missing ownership and lifetime relationship.
Trace where the object is created, who owns it, and which event ends its lifetime.
slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 9, use 9.3.1 Recognizing Lifetime-Related Bugs as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. A dangling pointer or reference does not become safe merely because it is nonnull. It may point to an object that has been destroyed, a vector element invalidated by reallocation, or a temporary whose lifetime ended. Checking the numeric address cannot reconstruct the missing ownership and lifetime relationship. Trace where the object is created, who owns it, and which event ends its lifetime. Then ask whether every use occurs before that event. A returned reference to a local fails this test immediately. Runtime sanitizers can reveal some executed lifetime defects, but absence of a report is not a proof. The design must make valid lifetimes understandable without relying on lucky memory contents. The graduate-level move is to ask what evidence would make the claim trustworthy: a compiler diagnostic, a runtime value, a preserved invariant, or a boundary that failed cleanly. slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 9, use Build a time-ordered object map as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. At the first call to persistent_next, the static object is initialized and then incremented. At the second call, that same object is incremented again. For local_next(10), the parameter and local result belong to that call; the returned value is eleven. After return, the local objects no longer serve as objects the caller may access. Inside the nested block, scoped is available and can be tested. Outside, its name is unavailable. The static counter still exists even though its name is not directly visible in main. These observations separate visibility from persistence without relying on implementation-specific memory addresses. keyPoints: Can a name be local while its object persists?
Yes.
A function-local static has a local name and persistent storage duration.

slides.narration: In this part of Chapter 9, use Review and solution reasoning as an engineering claim, not a vocabulary word. Can a name be local while its object persists? Yes. A function-local static has a local name and persistent storage duration. Does a reference universally extend lifetime? No. Some language constructs have specific extension rules, but a reference is not a general ownership mechanism. Why can returning a value be safer than returning a reference? The caller receives a result without needing the callee’s local object to remain alive. A reference requires a valid longer-lived target. Why is changing a local to static not always a proper fix? It changes sharing, persistence, and possibly concurrency behavior. A lifetime extension must still match the application’s intended state model. The graduate-level move is to ask what evidence would make the claim trustworthy: a compiler diagnostic, a runtime value, a preserved invariant, or a boundary that failed cleanly.
